title: Review: Principles of organisation; Animal tissues organs and organ systems
source: Questions and terms copied unchanged from the site's bank, except where marked for AQA GCSE Biology (8461) (status of the source: authored-gated-unreviewed). Terms and clues: 4.2.1-c03 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition; 4.2.2-c21 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition; 4.2.2-c19 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition; 4.2.2-c24 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition. Questions: 4.2.1-q01, 4.2.2-q04, 4.2.2-q13, 4.2.2-q15, 4.2.2-q18, 4.2.1-q02, 4.2.2-q07, 4.2.2-q12, 4.2.2-q16, 4.2.2-q02, 4.2.2-q11, 4.2.2-q17. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: organ
items.clue: An aggregation of tissues performing specific functions.

items.label: Vein
items.clue: A blood vessel that carries blood back towards the heart.

items.label: Pacemaker
items.clue: A group of cells located in the right atrium that controls the natural resting heart rate.

items.label: Plasma
items.clue: The liquid part of the blood, which transports the blood cells and dissolved substances around the body.

questions.stem: A structure in an organism is made up of several different tissues that work together to carry out a specific function. Which level of organisation is this structure?

options.text: a tissue, a group of similar cells
an organ system, a group of organs
an organ, an aggregation of tissues
an organism, a group of organ systems

questions.explanation: Correct: organs are aggregations of tissues performing specific functions, which is exactly what the structure described is.

questions.stem: Protease in the stomach works fastest at pH 2. What happens to its activity at pH 8?

options.text: It falls, as the active site changes shape.
It rises, as enzymes work best at about pH 7.
It falls, as the enzyme is killed by alkali.
It falls, as the enzyme has been used up.

questions.explanation: Away from its optimum pH the shape of the active site changes, so the substrate no longer fits and activity falls.

questions.stem: Which pairing of a blood vessel with its structure is correct?

options.text: Artery: thick wall resists the high pressure.
Vein: thick muscular wall resists high pressure.
Capillary: thick wall resists the blood pressure.
Artery: valves stop blood flowing backwards.

questions.explanation: An artery carries blood away from the heart at high pressure, so its wall is thick, with muscle and elastic fibres.

questions.stem: A photograph shows the cells in a sample of blood. Which statement is correct?

options.text: Platelets move around the blood and destroy pathogens.
Plasma is the liquid that carries oxygen to the cells.
Red blood cells have a nucleus that controls oxygen use.
Red blood cells have no nucleus, so they carry more oxygen.

questions.explanation: A red blood cell is adapted to its function of carrying oxygen: it has no nucleus, leaving more room for haemoglobin.

questions.stem: Why might an artificial heart be used for a patient with heart failure?

options.text: It keeps a patient alive while awaiting a donor.
It replaces a faulty valve inside the patient.
It cures the heart failure without any further care.
It lowers the level of cholesterol in the blood.

questions.explanation: Artificial hearts are occasionally used to keep patients alive whilst waiting for a heart transplant, or to allow the heart to rest as an aid to recovery.

questions.stem: Which statement about organ systems in a living organism is correct?

options.text: Organ systems are made of one organ with one function.
Organ systems are made of cells grouped together.
Organ systems are made of one tissue with a function.
Organ systems are made of organs that work together.

questions.explanation: Correct: organs are organised into organ systems, which work together to form organisms.

questions.stem: Which statement about digestive enzymes is correct?

options.text: Bile is the enzyme that breaks down fat droplets.
One enzyme is able to digest every type of food.
Protease is made in the stomach and pancreas.
Amylase is made only in the wall of the stomach.

questions.explanation: Protease is produced in the stomach, the pancreas and the small intestine, and it breaks down proteins to amino acids.

questions.stem: Which feature of the alveoli increases the rate of gaseous exchange?

options.text: A wide tube that carries air down to the lungs.
A thick outer wall that resists air pressure.
A supply of plasma that takes up the oxygen.
A large surface area and a good blood supply.

questions.explanation: The alveoli are adapted for gaseous exchange by a large surface area and the capillary network that surrounds them.

questions.stem: Which statement about the treatment of coronary heart disease is correct?

options.text: Statins are used to widen the blocked coronary arteries.
Stents are used to keep the coronary arteries open.
Stents are used to lower the level of blood cholesterol.
Artificial hearts are used to cure the heart disease.

questions.explanation: In coronary heart disease fatty material narrows the coronary arteries, and stents are used to keep them open.

questions.stem: Which statement describes the lock and key theory of enzyme action?

options.text: The enzyme fits into every kind of substrate.
The enzyme is used up by its own substrate.
The enzyme changes shape to fit any substrate.
The substrate fits the enzyme's active site.

questions.explanation: In the lock and key theory, used as a simplified model of enzyme action, the substrate is the key that fits the active site of the enzyme.

questions.stem: Which statement about the double circulatory system is correct?

options.text: Blood passes through the heart once each circuit.
Arteries carry blood with oxygen to the lungs.
The right ventricle pumps blood to the lungs.
The left ventricle pumps blood to the lungs.

questions.explanation: The right ventricle pumps blood to the lungs where gas exchange takes place, while the left ventricle pumps blood around the rest of the body.

questions.stem: A person has a heart valve that has developed a leak. Which statement is correct?

options.text: Blood flows backwards through the leaking valve.
The volume of blood pumped stays the same.
Only a heart transplant can treat the problem.
An artificial heart gives a permanent cure.

questions.explanation: A faulty valve that leaks lets blood flow backwards, so less blood is pumped forward to the body.
